summary: Boundary County cupola cabin on Queen Mountain, dated 1928 and abandoned around 1930 after lightning trouble; a 2020 photo visit found wreckage.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com and Rex's page list it as gone; a 2020 photo visit found wreckage that Peakbagging calls all that remains.

staffing.status: one name on firelookout.com (Victor Foss under 1933, role not stated); no other staffing in the sources read

access.note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists it as hike-in on Kaniksu National Forest land; no closure or permit is described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as hike-in.

events.note: 1914 newspaper item, quoted on Rex's page, names the Mt. Queen lookout as one of five lookout points, with telephone communications established to it
Cupola cabin; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1928, Peakbagging says around 1928
Idaho Fire Lookouts and Peakbagging give 1930; firelookout.com says the 1930s
firelookout.com lists Victor Foss under 1933; the page does not state a role, and the date conflicts with a 1930 abandonment

evidence.supports: 1928 cupola cabin; site abandoned in the 1930s for lightning; gone; 1933 Victor Foss
evidence.quote: 1928: cupola cabin. Site was abandoned in the 1930s when it was discovered to be an extreme lightning target. Gone. 1933: Victor Foss.

evidence.supports: about 13 miles north-northeast of Bonners Ferry
abandoned after two years as an extreme lightning target
evidence.quote: The site was abandoned after only 2 years when it was discovered to be an extreme lightning target.

evidence.supports: Kaniksu National Forest on the site's elevation line

evidence.quote: There will be one of the five lookout points on the Pend d'Oreille national forest locally known as the Mt. Queen lookout.

evidence.quote: At the present time telephone communications are established to the Mt. Queen lookout.

evidence.quote: Located in the Kaniksu National Forest

corrections.why: Three of four pages name the Kaniksu National Forest for the current site. Rex's page uses the Pend Oreille name, the same name as its 1914 item.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho Fire Lookouts and Peakbagging give 1930; firelookout.com says the 1930s and lists Victor Foss under 1933. Not resolved; the story gives the 1930 date and reports the 1933 entry as a conflict.

Three pages give 1928 for the cupola cabin, but a 1914 newspaper item quoted on Rex's page already names a Mt. Queen lookout with telephone communications. The sources do not say whether an earlier structure stood there. Not resolved; the story says so.
Kaniksu National Forest on three pages; Pend Oreille National Forest on Rex's page, which uses the same name as its 1914 item. The story uses Kaniksu.

notes_for_editor: Read firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts, Rex's page and Peakbagging.com (photo dated August 12, 2020). The 1928 build date appears on three pages; the abandonment year is the main conflict. Victor Foss appears only on firelookout.com; no other source was checked for him. Peakbagging credits Kresek for the lightning detail and mentions benchmark datasheet TO0911; neither was read. Access public is inferred from the hike-in label and national forest land. The brief's events had no 1928 build; added. The 1914 item says will be and at the present time, so the earlier lookout's status is unclear.
